properties.content:

Violation Code: 105.46(b) - IMPLEMENTATION OF EROSION AND SEDIMENTATION CONTROL PLANS – Permittee failed to conduct construction in a manner to minimize erosion of banks and bed of the stream and disturbance of the regimen of the stream.
Violation ID: 8269473
Permit API: 021-21034
Unconventional: No
County: Cambria
Municipality: Susquehanna Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 4/01/2026
Comments: An Administrative inspection is being conducted in response to Department review of the operator's email response to IR 4149963. The operator stated in their email response to IR 4149963 that they are obtaining outside expert assistance to address the stream crossing, and they will contact DEP Technical services as necessary. During the time of IR 4168004, the last surface inspection conducted on site, the stream bank of Kings Run upstream of the access road was heavily eroded and both inlets of the dual culvert were not observable. This may suggest that the dual culvert is restricting the flow of Kings Run, due to potential clogging and/or collapsing of the culvert inlets. No loose sediment was observed in Kings Run and water was observed flowing from the culvert outlets at the time of inspection.Upon conducting review and obtaining further clarification from the operator that they obtained the original stream crossing permit when they acquired this site, it appears that the operator has assumed responsibility for maintaining the eroded and deteriorated stream crossing. Therefore violations shall be issued in this Administrative inspection.

Comments: This administrative inspection report is in response to the receipt of analytical results for sample number 4406-018 collected on 12/12/2022 at 11:45AM as part of inspection report #3471637 at the Kingsley E Pad. Elevated levels of metals and chlorides in the sample analysis indicate a release of a pollutional substance.Sample 4406-018 indicated elevated concentrations of the following parameters: Barium - 3,025 mg/L; Strontium- 918.9 mg/L; Specific Conductivity- >12,890 micro-ohms/cm; Total Chloride- 29,135.3 mg/L. (Photo 1 and 2). The operator has already begun Act 2 site characterization on site based on CSL402(b) Potential Pollution violation within inspection report #3471637. According to the 15 day response submitted by Blackhill Energy on December 22, 2022 the following actions have been taken:Vac trucks dispatched to remove remaining fluid from puddles,The gas buster tank was moved and placed on new secondary containment,Potentially impacted pad construction material and soils with elevated conductivity have been excavated, placed in lined rolloffs, and staged on the pad.Moody and Associates is conducting confirmation EC screening of the excavation area and conducting waste characterization sampling of the impacted material. Violations noted.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 995319
Permit API: 051-23285
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Dunbar Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/11/2023
Comments: On May 11th 2023, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Nelson 2 OG Well. The findings were as follows:At the time of the inspection, the well appeared to be equipped for production. The well posting was present at the time of the inspection.The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. There were erosion and sedimentation issues onsite due to the pump jack actively releasing fluid onto the ground. There were observed leaks and discharge on the ground and around the wellhead. The Department observed the pump jack is actively releasing a fluid (where the pump jack enters the wellhead) to the ground. This active release is causing erosion to occur in the adjacent field. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the area as necessary in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy. The Department requests the operator provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. Soil conductivity readings were taken at 2 points on the site of the stained soil. The soil conductivity readings were out of range (above 20.00mS). Soil samples were also taken at three points(see photos 9,10,11). Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued. Additional violations maybe forthcoming pending further review of sampling results.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after multiple produced fluid releases on Pad B as well as sediment discharges from the access road. Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. On Pad B, the production equipment is still being installed the flow lines from the well heads to the production equipment. The electrical conductivity (EC) in the trench near the B-11H well head was 2.1 mS/cm. The EC of the puddles in the northeast corner of Pad B where the MASS was located is 575 uS/cm. The EC of the fluid is 2.09 mS/cm in the sump at the east outlet of the north stormwater channel. The fluid flowing out of the east outlet of the stormwater channel had an EC of 1.4 mS/cm. In the northcentral area of the well pad, the excavated trenches are still present. The EC of the fluid in the largest trench near the north stormwater channel was 1.4 mS/cm. The fluid in the excavated portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC of 2.02 mS/cm.The east side of the well pad was being back-filled with gravel during this inspection. The berm of the secondary containment for the frac tank on the east side of the well pad is damaged.On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. A battery of frac tanks are present within secondary.Violations remain outstanding against the ESCGP for the sediment discharges along the access road into the waters of the commonwealth.Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

The Department's assessment of the shared portion of this access road as well as the direct portion of this access road can be found in IR 4181625.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Armstrong 2 well site to be overgrown with vegetation, the Department recommends the Operator maintain the vegetation within the well site to ensure the well site remains accessible. A well tag was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted gas well with all required information posted on it and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the surface of the gas well at this time. A heavily rusted production tank was also observed on site and connected for production, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this tank at this time. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tank to ensure the corrosion does not worsen resulting in a release.Although no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed, a strong gas odor and hissing was observed to be coming from the lower portion of the gas wellhead, IR 4181625 documents the Department's request for OGI assistance to assess the integrity of the gas wellhead. While on site, the Department called Matt Anderson (listed as Managing Member in the Departments records for Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc), to notify them about the potential gas leak, however, Mr. Anderson stated he no longer manages Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc and provided the Department with an email address for Oil and gas Mgmt Inc. The Department then attempted to contact Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc again by calling the number on the well tag, however, this number was out of service. Violations are also being issued at this time for failure to have updated and accurate Operator information posted on site. Based on today's inspection, violations are being continued at this time for the heavily rusted production equipment due to their corrosion posing the risk of a spill and/or release and new violations are being issued for failure to have updated and accurate operator information on site.

Violation ID: 8274049
Permit API: 051-24570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: Redstone Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/06/2026
Comments: On May 6, 2026, the Department conducted a follow-up inspection to IR 4178322 at the Ritter well site in Redstone Township, Fayette County. Violations were issued in IR 4178322 for failure to conduct long-term maintenance on Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMPs), which appeared to be resulting in accelerated erosion and sedimentation on Tree Farm Road. Tree Farm Road is a township gravel road that connects to the site access road.The Department requested the NOV Response to IR 4178322 from the operator by May 7, 2026. An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on July 10, 2017.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of Tree Farm road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in an accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is on site (photo 2). Eight gas wells are onsite that appear to be equipped for production. Well 5H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photo 5). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection. The GPU units are not equipped with secondary containment. However, the gas wells on site were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of a fluid leak, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the GPU units (photos 6 and 7).The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 3 and 4). The severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation remains downslope of the well pad on Tree Farm Road (photos 14-24). The Department observed a rock-lined stormwater channel along the access road, which is located upslope of Tree Farm Road. This rock-lined stormwater channel appears to be in need of maintenance, as it appears to be nearly level with the access road (photo 25). Vegetation that appears to be flattened by recent stormwater washout was observed downslope of the rock-lined stormwater channel and at the eastern terminus of the riprap stormwater channel north of the well pad (photos 11-13). The riprap stormwater channel installed north of the well pad is located upslope of the most severely eroded portion of Tree Farm Road. Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4178322 shall remain outstanding.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC in Hamilton Township, McKean County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/31/2024 to PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC in Hamilton Township, McKean county. SWMA 610(2) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person constructed, altered, operated or utilized a solid waste storage, treatment, processing or disposal facility without a permit from DEP as required by the Solid Waste Management Act or in violation of the rules or regulations adopted under this act, or orders of DEP, or in violation of any term or condition of any permit issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/31/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 610(2) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person constructed, altered, operated or utilized a solid waste storage, treatment, processing or disposal facility without a permit from DEP as required by the Solid Waste Management Act or in violation of the rules or regulations adopted under this act, or orders of DEP, or in violation of any term or condition of any permit issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8212372
Permit API: 083-51666
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/31/2024
Comments: Upon being made aware of a crude oil release near this conventional well, I contacted Pennhills and learned that a steel gathering line located along the eastern side of the road (downslope of this well) was found to be compromised on December 9, 2024 and actions were taken to repair the line and remediate impacted media at that time. Since that time, Pennhills has decommissioned and vac'd out all fluid from the compromised line and are currently using a different gathering line that parallels the western edge of the road to carry fluids from this well and others located beyond this location. Representatives of Pennhills stated that the bulk of the earth disturbance along the eastern edge of the road was conducted to locate the portion of the line that was leaking and that they constructed an underflow dam downslope of the road to contain residual product that continues to leach from the road bank due to the abundance of larger rocks and roots in the area. Upon my arrival for this inspection, I observed the disturbed area along the eastern edge of the road that accesses this well. There was no visual evidence of crude oil across this disturbance, which was temporarily stabilized with seed and mulch. Downslope of the road, an approximate 20'x30' area had soil exposed due to Pennhills' reported removal of oil soaked leaves from the area. Isolated pockets of crude oil remain throughout this area, which drains towards the underflow dam that is located approximately 100' east of the well [41.82619 -78.85691]. The underflow dam is functioning and appears to be regularly maintained, as there is currently only a minor sheen atop the standing water behind it.Crude oil was also observed on the surface at a recessed area approximately 30' east (41.82632 -78.85674 [downslope]) of the underflow dam that appears to have migrated subsurface from the vicinity of the underflow dam to this point.A second area of oil soaked leaves/soil was discovered approximately 30' south (41.82607 -78.85661) of the underflow dam in a currently dry channel.At this time, the constructed underflow dam and continued use of absorbent diapers/booms appear to be sufficient containment measures. It is highly suggested to regularly monitor the containment and evaluate downslope of the impacted area, particularly during and after rain and snowmelt events.The quantity of product released was unknown, but appears to be less than one barrel at this time. No watercourses have impacted by this incident at this time. Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate if the current containment remains sufficient, if there was further migration of crude oil or evidence is presented that indicates the released quantity was greater than one barrel.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-06-25 to William H Brawand in Jones Twp, Elk county. 78.60(a) - DISCHARGE REQUIREMENTS - Operator discharged a substance into waters of the Commonwealth contrary to 25 Pa. Code Chapters 91, 93, 95 and 102, The Clean Streams Law and the 2012 Oil and Gas Act.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.60(a) - DISCHARGE REQUIREMENTS - Operator discharged a substance into waters of the Commonwealth contrary to 25 Pa. Code Chapters 91, 93, 95 and 102, The Clean Streams Law and the 2012 Oil and Gas Act.
Violation ID: 853696
Permit API: 047-25054
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-25
Comments: While drilling on 6/24, the operator encountered fresh water. Cement returns and drill cuttings ran down the location toward a stream. The operator dug two small pits to contain this water and solids in order to prevent discharge to the stream. Some of the dirt was pushed right to the edge of the stream. Rain overnight 6/24-25 allowed the pits to overflow and also caused sediment to run into the stream from the location and dirt piles. At the time of this inspection, the stream and pits were both colored with sediment, which could also be seen in a pond just downstream. Drilling will continue 6/26-27, after which the drilling contractor will empty the pits and backfill. It was suggested that they pump the water as far from the stream as possible and/or use a sediment filter bag to prevent any further discharge.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 992331
Permit API: 081-21879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/19/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after multiple releases occurred on Pad B. The wells on Pad B are in flowback. Secondary containment is installed surrounding the well heads. According to Zac Subra with EQT, earlier in the day less than 5 gallons of fluid was sprayed on the pad surface and onto the secondary containment around the well heads from a valve attached to a sand separator next to one of the well heads. The area of the pad surface had already been scraped by Tobias Machinery during this inspection. Some sand from the produced fluid spray was observed on the secondary containment.The sump remains installed at the northeast end of the north stormwater channel. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid in the sump was 2.60 mS/cm. Multiple seeps were observed coming from the well pad side slope and the topsoil stockpile which were flowing into the sump. The EC of this fluid was 3.55 mS/cm. The fluid coming from the seeps had a red/orange rust color to it. Mr. Subra said that EQT believes that the color is likely due to iron content in the soil. The fluid in the north central portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC between 3.55 to 3.76 mS/cm.Mr. Subra said that final samples have been taken for the Act 2 remediation report but that the sample results were not yet available as of the time of this inspection. Multiple evaporators are also in operation on Pad B. The secondary containment for the evaporators appears to be in good condition. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs appear to be in good condition.On Pad A, six wells are still in production. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. The access road and adjacent pipeline right-of-way appeared to be dry. No new sediment discharges were observed. Some of the stormwater culverts under the access road were partially filled with sediment. Comments: The DEP completed an administrative inspection on Tilden Bradford's Nichols 1H well (API 015-21167) located in Smithfield Township, Bradford County on 5/17/2021. The inspection was completed in order to summarize sample results from a sample collected during the 4/26/2021 inspection (IR #3182275). On 4/26/2021, I inspected Tilden Bradford's Nichols A well site and discovered elevated electrical conductivity (EC) puddles on the pad surface, outside of containment. Elevated EC puddles were field measured utilizing an Oakton PCSTestr 35 and ranged in EC from ~2.1mS/cm to ~4.87mS/cm. A sample for standard analysis code (SAC) 942 was collected on 4/26/2021 from a puddle field measured at ~4.87mS/cm. The sample was submitted to the DEP Laboratory in Harrisburg, PA on 4/27/2021 and the final sample results were reported on 5/15/2021. The DEP's analytical sample results are attached as photos and as a file. Additional information regarding the inspection can be found in inspection record #3182275. The operator later provided an email determining that the elevated EC water must have been from a water truck that had a spill in the offload area and then drove through it and onto the pad as they left. Remediation began as soon as the operator was notified. Based on the sample results of 0983-202 and the findings from inspection record #3182275, violations of the following are now cited against API # 015-21167: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 25 Pa. This inspection is being conducted in response to drilling notifications for six wells that were recently permitted at the site.When I arrived on site, I met JKLM's Terra Tokarz who accompanied me on the inspection. We started at JKLM's on-site office where the company man, Nick Peluso, explained current operations. A Highland rig has completed the surface sections to approximately 800 feet on all six wells. Secondary containment had been installed around the well cellars with drilling operations being conducted within the secondary containment. Five half-round dumpsters have been installed in secondary containment to collect drill cuttings. Drill cuttings are being solidified with wood chips. Two frac tanks and two 400-barrel tanks were installed on the north side of the pad, to be used for freshwater. Two 400-barrel tanks had been installed on the southeast side of the pad to be used for storing screened drilling water that had been used down hole. One 400-barrel tank has been installed on the southeast. Labels had fallen off of the 400-barrel tanks or were still being procured. Terra confirmed after the inspection that the missing labels were delivered to the site and all labels were securely attached. A 20' x 30' puddle of liquid in the area reported for a spill on 12/16/2025 field tested at 1460 uS conductance during this inspection. A 3' x 8' by half inch deep puddle of liquid southeast of the screened return water tanks on the unprotected pad surface field tested at 1780 uS conductance. Liquid on the unprotected pad surface in other areas of the pad field tested at 730 uS conductance or less.Temporary compost filter socks remain installed around the pad. Two sediment basins have been installed on the west side of the pad. They were adequately stabilized and appeared to be functioning as designed with a minimal amount of standing water. Due to snow cover, stabilization on the cut and fill slopes could not be assessed during this inspection. A small area of sloughing on the cut slope that was witnessed on a previous inspection remains but does not appear to be worsening. This is scheduled to be repaired as seasonal conditions allowed. Construction is scheduled but has not been initiated for an infiltration berm on the west side of the access road entrance, along Mitchell Creek Road.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 4110167 for puddles of fluid with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface.The DEP recommends monitoring the site for released fluids and elevated conductance liquids and removing as discovered.I departed the site at hours.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 9/17/2025 to EQT PROD CO in Morris Township, Greene county. 78a55(a) - CONTROL AND DISPOSAL PLANNING - PPC Plan - Person conducting oil and gas operations failed to prepare and implement a site specific PPC plans according to 25 Pa. Code §§ 91.34 and 102.5(l).
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 9/17/2025
Violation Code: 78a55(a) - CONTROL AND DISPOSAL PLANNING - PPC Plan - Person conducting oil and gas operations failed to prepare and implement a site specific PPC plans according to 25 Pa. Code §§ 91.34 and 102.5(l).
Violation ID: 8249208
Permit API: 059-27655
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Morris Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/17/2025
Comments: On 09/17/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the Harden Farms Well Site following receipt of an incident report that was submitted to the Department on 09/17/2025 at 12:17 (CTS 392314).It was reported that 10 gallons of biocide material was spilled on site at 12:00, 09/17/2025. No waterways were affected. It was also reported that a clean up crew (SPSI) was on site.I called the EQT representative who reported the spill, Lance Witters, for information. I noted that SPSI arrived after I did, and I requested the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) to be sent to me. It was described to me that the material spilled was a Multi-Chem biocide. The cause of the release was that a hose back pressured, biocide flowed back to the tank, and the tank overflowed. It was estimated that 10 gallons spilled.SPSI had not began remediation and was not on the pad when I arrived. No personal were on the pad upon my arrival.The following was observed:The contaminated area was adjacent to the gas production units (GPUs). It was unknown if any production fluid was present in addition to the biocide spilled; no elevated conductivity was observed. No remediation had begun and SPSI was not on the pad when I arrived on the pad. SPSI arrived to the site after the Department (Photo 1). An extremely strong odor was experienced on site in the vicinity of the contaminated area.SPSI then arrived on the pad and had not begun remediation while I was on site. The impacted area was located between the well heads and the GPUs. The impacted area appeared wet with small sections of pooled fluid (Photos 2-5).I asked SPSI if they had the SDS, and they did not. The SDS was not located on site with the site documents in the mailboxes. I was able to locate a Control and Disposal Plan and the Site Specific Safety and Environmental Plan and Policy. I was not able to locate any information related to the Multi-Chem biocide (Photos 6-9). I also did not find a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC) on site. The SDSs are required to be on site. The PPC Plan is also required to be on site during drilling or completion activities, however the well operator shall prepare and develop a site specific PPC plan prior to storing, using, or generating regulated substances to, on or from a well site.The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance (Photo 10).The Department requests a description of the activities that were being carried out that resulted in a spill.Due to the SDS not present on site, a PPC Plan not on site, failure to control regulated fluids with a release to the ground, and failure to use secondary containment, violations of 78a.54, 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(i)5iD, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78a64a(b) are being issued.

Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all five wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. The current Operator information has not yet been updated in the Department's electronic database. Well number 019-21931, along with four other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21907, 019-21928, 019-21929, 019-21932), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Although the Act Nine sign has been changed to reflect the current owner of the well location, the well tags have not yet been updated. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2139667, 2139736, 2139741, 2199744 and 2139746, (conducted on February 13, 2013), suggests that all of the wells have been stimulated. Subsequent inspections indicate that that the wells have been on inactive status since at least March of 2014. ESCGP number ESX11-019-0091 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 09/15/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. The location consists of one very large well location and a separate tank pad. The location is overgrown and clearly has not been tended to in any way for some time. There are currently, however, no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site.

Comments: The DEP conducted an incident response inspection of Repsol's DCNR 594 (02-207) well site located in Bloss and Hamilton Townships, Tioga County on 3/10/2020 at 1225 hours. The weather was 50 degrees with an overcast and rain. Ernie Shumbat represented Repsol onsite and oversaw excavation activities. Bishop Brothers Construction handled the excavation activities and Golder (environmental consultant) handled the environmental side of things. Repsol reported that a water truck had released approximately 20 gallons of produced water from a valve to the pad surface in front of the produced water offload area. The release had impacted the pad material directly in front of the offload area (see photo #3). Golder had tested the pad material for electrical conductivity (EC) and marked the area of impact. While I was onsite, Repsol was still waiting for an 811 call approval for excavation. While awaiting approval, excavation as deep as 12 inches was initiated. Impacted material was scraped up and placed in a lined roll-off container for disposal. Areas after the initial scrape were returned to normal soil EC readings (less than 1.0 mS/cm). The small area directly in front of the offload area (believed to absorb most of the release) was still reading high EC. I left the site around 1340 hours and rain had already began falling. Further excavation was conducted and a reported 7 yards of material was removed from the pad and placed in the roll-off container. Photos were provided by Repsol to show the completed excavation area. The area was backfilled and Repsol was awaiting disposal approval to properly dispose of the impacted material. Due to the observations made during the inspection and the timely response made by the operator, violations of the following were noted as immediately corrected against API # 117-22006: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 35 P.S. 6018.301 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a)

Impacted material was scraped up and placed in a lined roll-off container for disposal. Areas after the initial scrape were returned to normal soil EC readings (less than 1.0 mS/cm). The small area directly in front of the offload area (believed to absorb most of the release) was still reading high EC. I left the site around 1340 hours and rain had already began falling. Further excavation was conducted and a reported 7 yards of material was removed from the pad and placed in the roll-off container. Photos were provided by Repsol to show the completed excavation area. The area was backfilled and Repsol was awaiting disposal approval to properly dispose of the impacted material. Permit API: 063-31807
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Grant Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/20/2021
Comments: On 8/20/21 OGI J. Branan conducted a follow up inspection on PGE 37-063-31807 Marjorie C Yanity 1025 OG well. The water in the cellar is below the 11-3/4¿ x 16¿ casing. The gas bubbling is not visible due to the water level being below the top of the 11 ¿ ¾¿ by 16¿ casing annulus at the time of the inspection. Based on gas samples taken by Moody & Associates, and evaluation by ECHELON Applied Geosciences Consulting evaluations and interpretations, the gas is identified as lower Mississippian. ¿The gas in the 11-3/4¿ X 16¿ of the Yanity 1025 is likely associated with Lower Mississippi Formations in this area of the basin, possibly the Burgoon (Big Injun) sands.¿ (ECHELON Applied Geosciences Consulting) The Burgoon sands are approximately 400¿ to 500¿ deep. After reviewing ECHELONs evaluations and interpretations, and PGE 37-063-31807 1025 well completion report. Several coal seams and a couple freshwater aquafers were encountered before the casing seat of the surface string. There are freshwater aquafers noted on the well completion report at 83¿ and 130¿ and coal at 27¿ 83¿ 127¿ 152¿ 155¿ and 338¿. The depth of 11-3/4¿ casing is at 568.6¿, a couple hundred feet below the deepest coal. The report identifies the gas source behind the surface casing and a potential to comingle with the identified water aquifers. The Department is denying PGE any request to vent the gas from the 11-3/4¿ x 16¿ annulus as a permeant repair solution. As per 78.86 PGE is required to submit a plan to remediate the issue and has failed to do so. Also, within 30 days of receiving the inspection report, the Department is requesting any Logs or previous predrill data associated with the well.
